transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I keep hearing voices. I work as a nursing assistant, and lately, I hear them coming from the call-light speaker, or sometimes the hallway vents. They keep telling me which patient records have been changed. 

It's just as clear as somebody standing right next to me. Even when the unit is completely quiet and nobody else hears a thing... I still hear them.
Have you ever felt like people are trying to communicate with you through the TV, radio, or other objects, or that you have special abilities others don't?

Well, not through the TV or radio, no. But I do notice things that other people completely miss. 

Like at work... I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn't want anyone to see. I brought it up, and my supervisor tried to brush it off, saying it's just late entries or coding mistakes. But I know what I'm looking at. I can tell they're watching what I write in the system now, specifically because I'm the one who actually caught it.
Do you feel like you're being targeted or singled out because of what you've discovered, or that you have a special role or mission that others don't understand?

No, I wouldn't say it's a special mission or anything like that. I'm just a nursing assistant trying to do my job. I don't feel like I have some sort of special role that other people don't understand... I just happen to be the person who noticed the pattern with the charts. 

And I don't necessarily feel like I'm being targeted or singled out to be punished, um, I just know they're keeping a very close eye on my system entries now because I'm the one who spoke up about it to my supervisor. That's really all it is.
Do you ever feel like everyday events, like things you see or hear, have a special meaning that's directed at you, even if it doesn't involve a mission or being targeted?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't see special meanings in random things. It's really just the voices from the call-lights and the vents, and knowing what's going on with the charts at work. Everyday stuff is just everyday stuff to me.

Do you believe that the changes in the wound-care charts are being made intentionally to hide something, and if so, do you think this is part of a deliberate effort by management or someone else at work?

Yes, absolutely. It's definitely intentional. I mean, my supervisor tried to brush it off, like I said, telling me it's just late entries or coding mistakes. But I know what I'm looking at. I've been doing this a long time. 

Management doesn't want anyone to see the pattern in those wound-care charts. I don't know exactly what they're trying to hide, but they are deliberately covering something up. And because I'm the one who actually caught it and brought it up, I know they're watching exactly what I write in the system now. They're monitoring my entries because I figured it out.

latest_inference.note: The patient's persistent delusional beliefs about intentional alterations in wound-care charts and being monitored at work, along with auditory hallucinations limited to specific contexts, suggest a delusional disorder. Schizophrenia (F20.0, F20.3) is less likely due to absence of broader symptom criteria. Acute and transient psychotic disorders (F23.0, F23.8) are ruled out due to chronic nature of symptoms.

Ruled out some acute and transient psychotic disorders (e.g., F23.2, F23.3) due to chronic nature of symptoms. Still considering schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders with emphasis on auditory hallucinations and non-bizarre delusions of persecution or observation.
